searchText: it looks like the deposit cli tool follows EIP 2334 but it would be fairly straightforward to modify the code to do what you wanted Is there a way to determine what the widthdraw public key is for a validator deposit? Oh it looks like maybe beaconscan presents that info once it is processed in the beacon chain withdrawal pubkey is not published in the deposit. Instead, a SHA-256 hash of the pubkey is included Since there may be different withdrawal methods, it's just a digest of the necessary information So if I know the pub key, I can sha256 it and validate it's correct against the "withdraw_credentials"? A prefix byte in this 32 byte "withdrawal credentials" is used to determine the type of withdrawal. Right now there's only the pubkey type Yes, it's outlined in the spec that accompanies the deposit contract. I'll get you a link https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/v0.12.3/specs/phase0/deposit-contract.md#withdrawal-credentials hmmm I'm not having much luck figuring this out. Pubkey is hex string `0xblah` but `sha256(bytes[] blah)` looks nothing like `withdrawal_credentials` pretty sure I'm missing a step lol i'm a shitty coder so, sorry up front haha ethdo is converting the `bytes[] pub` to `var key bls.PublicKey` with `key.Deserialize(pub);` That's where I get lost plus trying to do it in python 🙂 I think I figured it out from the eth2.0-deposit-cli tool 🥳
